item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-26
item.description: Two documents published within a week describe two completely different ways of turning a Chinese open-source community into an institution, and neither has been read against the other. On the first: the OpenAtom Foundation publishes its donation ladder on a public web page with hard numbers — Outstanding Donor at no less than CNY 10 million a year, Platinum at no less than CNY 3 million a year with a binding commitment to give for at least three consecutive years, Gold at no less than CNY 1 million a year over two years, Silver at CNY 200,000 a year — and on 2026-11-20 in Zhengzhou it handed out nine new donor plaques: two Platinum, two Gold, five Silver. The foundation's own 2026-06-25 account counts 198 cumulative donors, 48 honoured on stage that day, 10 newcomers in 2026 and 12 renewals. On the second: on 2026-11-14 and 15, the eleventh China Open Source Conference (COSCon'26) opened in Hangzhou's Xihu district under a theme of 'the open source next generation', organised by the community body KAIYUANSHE and the AI learning community Datawhale, under the guidance of a municipal AI open-source academy, with the Xihu district party committee talent office and a science-city management committee as supporters. No ministry appears in the organiser line. The first document prices participation and publishes the price. The second distributes standing by contribution and gets absorbed by a city government that wants to recognise it in policy. Both are institutional designs. Only one of them has a published constitution, and it is the one that has no code.
